name: Monarch Money
tagline: Personal finance dashboard for budgeting, transactions, goals, and net worth

pricing.notes: Official pricing page checked; 2026 public references list $14.99/month or $99.99/year for Core.

tiers.name: Core
tiers.limits: One household; budgeting, goals, cash flow, net worth and account tracking

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Everything in Core plus forecasting, business tracking, advanced investment analysis, gains/losses and estate-planning features
tiers.notes: Annual only at $199/year; 7-day trial; desktop-first features.

pricing.billingTerms: Core monthly + annual; Plus annual only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Taxes may apply; app-store billing terms can differ. Core promotions do not apply to Plus or monthly plans. Plus is unavailable on advisor-sponsored accounts.

verdictSummary: A manual finance dashboard is buildable, but high-quality bank aggregation, transaction cleaning, investment data, household collaboration, and mobile sync make it real work.
coreLoopDIY: Import transactions from CSV or Plaid, categorize spending, track accounts/goals/net worth, and show monthly reports.
requirements: bank aggregation API or CSV import
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because personal finance apps are only valuable when data arrives automatically and safely.

priorArt.name: Firefly III
priorArt.desc: Open-source personal finance manager for budgets, transactions, and reports.

alternatives.name: Wealthfolio
alternatives.desc: Investments, net worth, spending, budgets and goals on your device; automatic broker sync is the paid shortcut.

facts.install: Native desktop or iOS app, or the official Docker image/Compose deployment for web mode
facts.dataFormat: Desktop and self-hosted modes use a local SQLite database (the web server exposes a configurable app.db path); optional Wealthfolio Connect and encrypted device sync send selected holdings/account data through the vendor service.
facts.gapVsPaid: Wealthfolio's free local mode lacks Monarch's turnkey multi-institution sync, household collaboration, automatic transaction cleanup, recurring detection, and integrated goal planning.

alternatives.name: Actual Budget
alternatives.desc: Budgets, imported transactions, schedules and reports on your disk; investment analytics are much thinner.

facts.install: Native desktop app for local-only use, or the official Docker/Node server for browser access and device sync
facts.dataFormat: Each client works from a local SQLite budget; the server keeps account metadata plus budget blobs under its data directory, and optional end-to-end encryption covers budget contents but not bank-sync tokens.
facts.gapVsPaid: Actual has much weaker investment and net-worth analytics and no equally seamless household collaboration or managed multi-provider account aggregation.

alternatives.name: Firefly III
alternatives.desc: Transactions, budgets, goals and net worth in Docker; portfolio analysis is not its favourite spreadsheet.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose deployment; a separate Firefly III Data Importer is normally added for bank files
facts.dataFormat: Transactions, accounts, budgets, rules, and metadata live in the configured MariaDB/MySQL or PostgreSQL database; uploads and generated files live in persistent server volumes.
facts.gapVsPaid: Firefly III requires server administration and is weaker than Monarch for investment tracking, household collaboration, polished goals, automatic institution sync, and mobile usability.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is operating a real web service, Docker, a database, application secrets, TLS, mail, backups, upgrades, and usually the separate importer plus an API token.

alternatives.name: FreeBudget
alternatives.desc: Budgets, rules, CSV imports, reports and net worth for free; live bank links cost extra.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser or installation of its progressive web app
facts.dataFormat: Transactions, budgets, rules, reports, and net-worth records live in FreeBudget's cloud; manual and CSV import/export are available, while linked-account data passes through Plaid when the paid sync option is enabled.
facts.gapVsPaid: FreeBudget's free tier relies on manual or CSV imports and has thinner investment, collaboration, goal, and mobile experience than Monarch's continuously synced household dashboard.

notes: Good kinda: spreadsheet replacement is yes, bank-sync product is harder.
prompt:
Build me a CSV-first personal finance dashboard to replace Monarch Money. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on localhost:4910, server-rendered pages with
  Chart.js for the graphs.
- Import bank and card CSV exports: per-bank column mapping saved after the first
  import, dedupe on a date+amount+description hash so re-imports are always safe.
- Rule-based categorization: substring or regex on description sets the category,
  rules run on import, and a fast keyboard-driven screen clears the leftovers.
- Monthly budget targets per category with actual-vs-budget bars and overspend
  flags, plus a cash-flow view by month.
- An accounts table including manual balances for things without CSVs (pension,
  property); a net-worth chart built from balance snapshots I enter monthly.
- A recurring-charge detector: same merchant, similar amount, monthly cadence,
  listed with annualized cost. That is the subscription-audit view.
- Everything local in one SQLite file, no bank credentials anywhere, no accounts,
  no telemetry. Nightly DB copy to backups/, keep 30.
- Out of scope: automatic bank sync via Plaid, household multi-user, and mobile
  apps. The monthly CSV ritual is the price of keeping credentials out of this.
- README: import walkthrough for two example bank CSV formats, backup location.
